finding.summary: When p.grad is not None and torch.any(p.grad != 0): If all parameter gradients are zero, ConstraintCheck.true(nonzero, ...) raises, aborting the backward step ('Gradients are all zero. Cannot make progress.'). (nnsmith/materialize/torch/symbolnet.py:188)
finding.review_note: blind review by an LLM subagent (round 1), not human: Zero gradients raise ConstraintError, grad_input_gen breaks and returns None, so for such models the gradient search gives up and make_oracle ends up using random inputs.

analysis.tier_note: the probes confirm what the Finding says
analysis.reasoning: The shown code gates a nonzero-gradient flag on `p.grad is not None and torch.any(p.grad != 0)`, then calls `ConstraintCheck.true(...)` with the zero-gradient error message. Thus all-zero gradients make the check fail and raise, matching the finding. The paper instead says to reinitialize and continue OUTER, so the abort behavior is an undisclosed discrepancy.
analysis.would_confirm: Run backward on a network with all parameter gradients zero and observe whether it raises the zero-gradient ConstraintError instead of reinitializing and continuing.
